title: The Church's Faith, Priests and Deacons
english: I give Him faith, and He gives me the kingdom (Song of Songs 6:3). He pastures in the purity of the Scriptures and of the holy doctrines. Turn your eyes away from those who disobey you (Song of Songs 6:5), and incline them toward me; for they, he says, have stirred up love in me.

'The work of a craftsman' (Song of Songs 7:1): by 'craftsman' he means Christ the Creator; for as He became obedient (Philippians 2:8), so has the Church. He speaks also of her chastity and her submission: her soul is subject to faith, and her body to chastity.

He shows her priesthood too, when he says, 'not lacking mixed wine' (Song of Songs 7:2), that is, the blood of Christ; for this is in the hands of the priests. Her neck (Song of Songs 7:4) he calls the deacons of Christ, because they carry Christ, the head of the Church. For they carry His holy body with a pure conscience (1 Timothy 3:9), confessing His mysteries.
translator_notes: Copy-text: PG 69; Fragmenta in Canticum canticorum (Greek). Original English from the Greek; no English base used.
The Greek of this section opens with 'λογισμοῖς ἐμποιοῦντος', the end of the sentence that begins in the previous section; those two words are translated there.
The last sentence runs across the section break ('…ἐν | καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει, ὁμολογοῦντες αὐτοῦ τὰ μυστήρια'); it is translated whole here, and the next section begins with the next sentence.

Song verses use English numbering. Chapter 6 numbers are the same in the LXX and English; in chapter 7 the LXX (with the Hebrew) runs one verse ahead (LXX 7:2, 7:3, 7:5 = English 7:1, 7:2, 7:4). 'I give Him faith, and He gives me the kingdom' glosses 'I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine; he pastures among the lilies' (Song of Songs 6:3); the lilies are read as the purity of the Scriptures.

'αὐτοὶ γὰρ … τὴν ἀγάπην ἐξήγειράν μοι [cod. σε]': PG prints μοι and records the manuscript reading σε ('in you'). The English follows the printed μοι; the variant is kept here in the notes, not in the reader text.

'διὰ τὸν Χριστὸν βαστάζειν τῆς Ἐκκλησίας τὴν κεφαλήν': read as 'because they carry Christ, the head of the Church' (τὸν Χριστόν as object, τὴν κεφαλήν in apposition), which the next sentence ('they carry His holy body') confirms. A reading 'for Christ's sake they carry the head of the Church' is grammatically possible but fits the context less well.
'with a pure conscience … mysteries' echoes Paul's rule for deacons, 'holding the mystery of the faith with a pure conscience' (1 Timothy 3:9).
baehrens: PG 69; Fragmenta in Canticum u03 rem early

title: The Royal Priesthood and the Savior's Coming
english: That is why he called it ivory: such deacons as Paul calls dignified, not given to much wine (1 Timothy 3:8).

'A king bound in the galleries' (Song of Songs 7:5). Or, taken another way, he says that the bond of the peoples' love is brought into a royal priesthood (1 Peter 2:9). Or else, 'in your delight' (Song of Songs 7:6) means in your love, because some are reckoned even among the righteous themselves.

The breasts are likened to clusters (Song of Songs 7:7), clusters that hold spiritual gladness. Or it means that I bring the confession, and 'His turning is toward me' (Song of Songs 7:10), either at the second coming, or also from the people of the Jews. So the bride's food is made holy, since Christ feasts with her.

That is, the Church prays that the Savior may come to dwell in Judea, by the providence of the One who gives Him to mankind, so that He may nurse at the breast of the Mother of God (Song of Songs 8:1).
translator_notes: Copy-text: PG 69; Fragmenta in Canticum canticorum (Greek). Original English from the Greek; no English base used.

The Greek of this section opens with 'καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει, ὁμολογοῦντες αὐτοῦ τὰ μυστήρια', the end of a sentence translated whole in the previous section. It closes with 'Εὑροῦσά', the first word of the lemma 'Εὑροῦσά σε' (Song of Songs 8:1), which is translated in the next section.

'Βασιλεὺς δεδεμένος ἐν παραδρομαῖς' follows the LXX of Song of Songs 7:6 (English 7:5); παραδρομαί, literally 'runnings' or 'galleries', is rendered 'galleries'. The comment that explains the first reading has dropped out of the catena; only the alternative ('Or, taken another way') survives.
'διὰ τό τινα καὶ αὐτῶν τῶν δικαίων νομίζεσθαι' is obscure in this condensed fragment; rendered literally, 'because some are reckoned even among the righteous themselves'.
'τοῖς ἔχουσι' agrees with τοῖς βότρυσιν, so the clusters are what hold spiritual gladness.
'Ἢ ὅτι ἐγὼ τὴν ὁμολογίαν προσάγω, καὶ ἐπ' ἐμὲ ἡ ἐπιστροφὴ αὐτοῦ' glosses Song of Songs 7:11 LXX (English 7:10), 'I am my beloved's, and his turning is toward me'.
'So the bride's food is made holy' has no surviving lemma; it may refer to the stored fruits of Song of Songs 7:13, but no reference is added in the text.

'τοῦ διδόντος αὐτόν' answers the LXX of Song of Songs 8:1, 'Who would give you (τίς δῴη σε) as my brother, nursing at my mother's breasts'. 'The One who gives Him' means God, so it is capitalized. 'θηλάσῃ τὴν Θεοτόκον' (literally 'that He may suck the God-bearer') is rendered 'nurse at the breast of the Mother of God'.
Song verses use English numbering (LXX 7:6, 7:7, 7:8, 7:11 = English 7:5, 7:6, 7:7, 7:10).
baehrens: PG 69; Fragmenta in Canticum u03 rem mid

title: The Vineyard, the Gardens and the Bride's Last Prayer
english: 'Finding you' (Song of Songs 8:1): that is, outside Jerusalem, where He was crucified (Hebrews 13:12). Or he means the burial that Joseph and Nicodemus provided (John 19:38–40). By pomegranates (Song of Songs 8:2) he means the saints. 'Its encircling walls are walls of fire' (Song of Songs 8:6): the walls of the Church, he says, are fire.

The spiritual Solomon came to have a vineyard (Song of Songs 8:11), and he means the Church. Baal-hamon means 'among those who have believed'. And who are the ones who have believed, if not those who received His commandments?

The one who sits in the gardens (Song of Songs 8:13) watches over the Churches. The companions listen, and they do not judge; rather, the Son does all the judging (John 5:22). The bride longs to hear, 'Enter into the joy of your Lord' (Matthew 25:21). She also asks Him to cast out the wicked, and by saying 'Flee' (Song of Songs 8:14) she asks Him to come to the saints.
translator_notes: Copy-text: PG 69; Fragmenta in Canticum canticorum (Greek). Original English from the Greek; no English base used.
The lemma 'Εὑροῦσά σε' ('finding you', Song of Songs 8:1 LXX: 'finding you outside, I would kiss you') is split across the section break; both words are translated here.
'Or he means the burial that Joseph and Nicodemus provided': ἤνεγκεν, literally 'brought', recalls the myrrh and aloes Nicodemus brought and the linen Joseph supplied (John 19:38–40).
'Ῥοῶν δὲ λέγει τῶν ἁγίων' glosses 'the juice of my pomegranates' (Song of Songs 8:2 LXX).

'Περίπτερα αὐτῆς, περίπτερα πυρός' follows the LXX of Song of Songs 8:6 (English 'its flashes are flashes of fire'). Cyril takes περίπτερα in its architectural sense, the structure that runs round a building, which is why he glosses it as the walls of the Church; it is rendered 'encircling walls' so the gloss makes sense.
'Βεελαμών' is the LXX form of Baal-hamon (Song of Songs 8:11); the name is given in its usual English spelling.
'τὴν κρίσιν πᾶσαν ὁ Υἱὸς ποιεῖ' recalls John 5:22, 'the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son'.
'Enter into the joy of your Lord' is Matthew 25:21 (repeated in 25:23).

'Ἀξιοῖ δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ τοὺς πονηροὺς ἐκβαλεῖν, Φύγε, λέγουσα, ἐπὶ τοὺς ἁγίους ἐλθεῖν': both infinitives depend on ἀξιοῖ, so she asks Him to cast out the wicked and to come to the saints. Song of Songs 8:14 bids the beloved flee 'upon the mountains of spices'; Cyril reads those mountains as the saints.
The stray '5' at the end of the Greek section is a page or column number from the print and is not translated.
baehrens: PG 69; Fragmenta in Canticum u03 rem close
